# Company Fundamentals

## Data Type

Company fundamentals are the line items reported in a firm's periodic financial statements (10-K annual filings, 10-Q quarterly filings, or non-US equivalents).

Fundamentals span three statements

- Income Statement (revenue, expenses, earnings)
- Balance Sheet (assets, liabilities, equity)
- Cash Flow Statement (operating, investing, financing flows)

Typically reported at

- Quarterly
- Annual

Compustat also flags whether a period is "as originally reported" or has since been restated.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why it Matters

- Items like revenues and costs are the foundation of discounting
- Fundamentals are the primary input to valuation models (DCF, comparables, residual income)
- They are combined into financial ratios used for screening and factor construction
- Central to credit analysis, covenant monitoring, and default prediction
- Drive academic research on earnings surprises, accruals, and accounting-based anomalies
- Basis for forensic/fraud-detection analysis

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data Structure

Unit of observation: one company in one fiscal period (quarter or year)

Primary identifiers

- GVKEY — Compustat's permanent company identifier
- CUSIP / Ticker
- Datadate — fiscal period end date
- Fiscal Year (FYEARQ) / Fiscal Quarter (FQTR)

Column Definitions (selected core items):

| Variable | Compustat Mnemonic | Description |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|
| Revenue | REVTQ | Total revenue for the period |
| Cost of Goods Sold | COGSQ | Direct costs of producing goods/services sold |
| SG&A | XSGAQ | Selling, general, and administrative expenses |
| Operating Income | OIADPQ | Operating income after depreciation |
| Net Income | NIQ | Bottom-line earnings attributable to common shareholders |
| Total Assets | ATQ | Sum of all assets on the balance sheet |
| Total Liabilities | LTQ | Sum of all liabilities |
| Cash & Equivalents | CHEQ | Cash and short-term investments |
| Long-Term Debt | DLTTQ | Long-term debt outstanding |
| Shareholders' Equity | SEQQ | Book value of common equity |
| CapEx | CAPXY | Capital expenditures, fiscal-year-to-date |

Structure

- One company: Rows = fiscal periods \| Columns = line items
- Multi-company panel: Rows = firm-period \| Columns = line items
- Temporal ordering: Convention is oldest to youngest

Reporting considerations

- Datadate reflects the fiscal period end, not the announcement/filing date
- Fiscal year-ends differ across companies (not all firms use a calendar year)
- Restatements: a later filing can revise an earlier period's figures — "as originally reported" and "as currently reported" can differ
- Point-in-time caution: using currently-reported (restated) fundamentals to explain historical stock prices introduces look-ahead bias

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Providers

### Institutional Research Databases

| Provider | Notes |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Compustat (via WRDS)** | Industry standard for academic fundamentals research; North America and Global |
| Refinitiv / LSEG Worldscope | Global fundamentals coverage |
| FactSet Fundamentals | Institutional-grade; widely used on the buy-side/sell-side |
| Bloomberg (FA screen) | Fundamentals integrated with terminal analytics |

### Public / Free Sources

| Provider | Notes |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| SEC EDGAR | Original source filings (10-K/10-Q); free but unstructured |
| Company Investor Relations sites | Original source; no cross-company standardization |
| stockanalysis.com, macrotrends | Free, limited history and customization |

Throughout this course, WRDS/Compustat is our primary source because it is standardized, survivorship-bias-free, and point-in-time flagged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Access Methods

- API
- Web GUI
- Batch jobs (on WRDS server)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Example Analyses

- Compute growth rates (YoY, QoQ) in revenue and earnings
- Screen for value, quality, or growth characteristics from raw fundamentals
- Construct the Piotroski F-Score or Altman Z-Score
- Estimate implied cost of capital / DCF valuations
- Study earnings-announcement drift and accounting-based anomalies
- Build credit risk / covenant monitoring models
- Benchmark a company against its peer group

# Expectations

## Data Type

Analyst expectations data capture Wall Street's forward-looking forecasts of a company's future performance — most commonly EPS, but also revenue and other line items — along with buy/sell/hold recommendations.

Reported at two levels

- Detail: each individual analyst's forecast
- Summary: consensus statistics aggregated across analysts (mean, median, standard deviation, number of estimates)

Forecast horizons include quarterly (Q1–Q4), annual (FY1, FY2), and long-term growth (LTG)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why it Matters

- Asset pricing is prospective
- Consensus estimates are the benchmark against which "earnings surprises" are measured
- Revisions in analyst forecasts are a widely studied predictor of returns
- Support implied cost-of-capital and forward-looking valuation models
- Analyst dispersion is a common proxy for uncertainty/disagreement among market participants

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data Structure

Unit of observation: one analyst's forecast for one company, for one forecast period, as of one statistical period (detail); or one company/forecast-period/statistical-period consensus (summary)

Primary identifiers

- Ticker / CUSIP
- Forecast Period End Date (FPEDATS) — the future date the forecast pertains to
- Statistical Period Date (STATPERS) — the date the consensus snapshot was taken
- Forecast Period Indicator (FPI) — Q1–Q4, FY1, FY2, LTG

Column Definitions (Summary Statistics file):

| Variable    | Description                                     |
|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| MEDEST      | Median forecast across contributing analysts    |
| MEANEST     | Mean forecast across contributing analysts      |
| STDEV       | Standard deviation across analyst forecasts     |
| NUMEST      | Number of analysts contributing to the estimate |
| ACTUAL      | Realized/reported value, once known             |
| ANNDATS_ACT | Date the actual value was announced             |

Structure

- Long panel: Rows = company × forecast period × statistical period \| Columns = estimate statistics
- STATPERS advances on a regular cadence (typically weekly) while FPEDATS is fixed, so a single forecast period accumulates many consensus snapshots as the period approaches
- Missing ACTUAL / ANNDATS_ACT values indicate the forecast period hasn't occurred yet (see the Exercise)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Providers

- IBES is the primary aggregator of Wall Street "consensus"

| Provider | Notes |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **LSEG I/B/E/S (via WRDS)** | Industry-standard academic source for consensus estimates |
| Zacks Investment Research | Commercial consensus estimates and rankings |
| FactSet Estimates | Institutional-grade; integrated with FactSet workstation |
| Visible Alpha | Granular, line-item-level consensus modeling |
| Bloomberg (EEO) | Estimates integrated within the Bloomberg terminal |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Access Methods

- WRDS Web GUI (Summary History / Detail History)
- WRDS batch/cloud queries
- Vendor terminals and APIs (FactSet, Bloomberg, Refinitiv Workspace)
- Unlike price or factor data, open R/Python packages for consensus estimates are limited; most access runs through subscription platforms

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Example Analyses

- Compute earnings surprises (actual − consensus)
- Study post-earnings-announcement drift conditioned on surprise magnitude
- Measure analyst forecast dispersion as an uncertainty proxy
- Track consensus revisions over time
- Build implied cost-of-capital estimates
- Compare forecast accuracy across analysts or brokerage houses

# Ratios

## Data Type

Financial ratios standardize relationships between financial statement items — and, in some cases, market prices — into metrics used to assess valuation, profitability, liquidity, leverage, and efficiency.

WRDS distributes ratios at two levels

- Firm-level: one ratio value per company per period
- Industry-level: ratios aggregated (mean/median) across all firms in a GICS classification

Common ratio categories

- Valuation (?)
- Profitability (?)
- Liquidity (current ratio, quick ratio)
- Leverage / Solvency (debt/equity, interest coverage)
- Efficiency (asset turnover, inventory turnover)

Typically reported at

- Monthly (firm-level ratios that combine market price with quarterly financials)
- Quarterly / Annual (fundamentals-only ratios)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Why it Matters

?

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data Structure

Unit of observation

- Firm-level: one company in one period
- Industry-level: one GICS classification (Sector / Industry Group / Industry) in one period, aggregated across constituent firms

Primary identifiers

- Firm-level: GVKEY / PERMNO / Ticker, Date
- Industry-level: GICS code, Date

Column Definitions (selected):

| Variable      | Description                          |
|:--------------|:-------------------------------------|
| P/E           | Price-to-earnings ratio              |
| P/B           | Price-to-book ratio                  |
| EV/EBITDA     | Enterprise value to EBITDA           |
| ROE           | Return on equity                     |
| ROA           | Return on assets                     |
| Current Ratio | Current assets / current liabilities |
| Debt/Equity   | Total debt / shareholders' equity    |

Structure

- Long panel: Rows = firm (or industry) × date \| Columns = ratio
- Industry-level files report whichever aggregation statistic is chosen at query time — mean or median (see the Exercise)
- Because many ratios combine market price with lagged accounting data, the same point-in-time and look-ahead considerations from Company Fundamentals apply here

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Providers

| Provider | Notes |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| **Financial Ratios Suite (via WRDS)** | Firm-level and industry-level; built by WRDS from Compustat, CRSP, and IBES |
| Bloomberg | Ratio screens integrated into the terminal (FA, EQS) |
| FactSet | Ratio and screening tools within the workstation |
| Morningstar Direct | Strong fund and equity ratio coverage |
| Public screeners (stockanalysis.com, macrotrends) | Free, limited history and customization |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Access Methods

- WRDS Web GUI (Financial Ratios Suite)
- WRDS batch/cloud queries
- Can also be computed manually by combining Compustat fundamentals with CRSP prices and IBES estimates

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Example Analyses

- Relative valuation screens (compare a firm's ratios to industry benchmarks)
- Construct value/quality factor portfolios from ratio data
- Track industry-level valuation cycles over time
- Credit scoring and covenant monitoring
- Peer/comparable-company benchmarking
